h1: Video production for Los Angeles brands, made remotely: motion graphics, animation and AI video
intro: We make video for established Los Angeles companies without a film crew: motion graphics, explainers, 2D and 3D animation, short-form edits for social, and clearly labeled AI video reviewed by a person. We also edit footage your own crew shoots, and can run a managed editing team when your content calendar outgrows your staff.

sections.h: First, what we do not do
p: Los Angeles is full of camera crews, studios and directors, and we are not trying to be another one. We do not send a crew to your set, and we will not claim a local studio. If your project needs live-action filming, you hire a crew or production company you trust, and we take it from there.

What we do is the work that does not need a camera in LA: animation, motion design, editing, AI-generated scenes and the steady volume of short videos that marketing teams now need every week. That is the honest shape of our video production. Los Angeles clients use us alongside their own shoots, not instead of them.

sections.h: Who in LA hires a remote video team
list: Fashion and beauty brands that need a constant stream of product reels, ad variants and launch teasers between bigger shoots
Entertainment and media companies that need extra editing hands, social cut-downs or animated title packages around a release
Health tech, aesthetics and dental practices that need treatment explainers and patient education animation instead of filming patients
Aerospace and engineering firms that need technical animation for trade shows, investor decks and recruiting, without filming sensitive facilities
Real estate developers that need animated walkthroughs and launch films for buildings that are not finished yet
p: The common thread among companies that hire a remote video team is volume and variety. A single campaign now needs a hero video, a dozen cut-downs, vertical and square versions, captions and a few ad variations to test. Booking a crew for each of those makes no sense, but someone still has to make them well and on time.

sections.h: AI video, done carefully in the home of the industry
p: Los Angeles is where the debate about AI in film and television is loudest, and for good reason. Union agreements now cover the use of performers' digital replicas, and California has passed laws on contracts for them. We take that seriously.

Our rules: we never create a likeness of a real person without their written consent, AI-generated content is labeled, a person reviews every output before it goes out, and we keep records of the tools and sources used. For most brands, AI video works best for ad variations, backgrounds and scenes that would be costly to film, not for replacing people on camera.

sections.h: Remote editing on an LA schedule
p: We work from London with specialists across several time zones. London is 8 hours ahead of Los Angeles most of the year, so footage uploaded at the end of your day can be cut overnight, with a first edit waiting for review in the morning. Feedback comes through time-coded comments, and calls go in your morning when a conversation is quicker. Large files move through cloud transfer, so nothing waits for a courier. If a project needs us in person, we plan a visit when the project needs it.

sections.h: Proof: deadlines that do not move
p: We run a managed video editing team for a US client, briefed and quality-checked through one lead. Our live work sharpens that discipline: we have run and broadcast more than 20 large-scale live events, where the date never moves.

faqs.q: Do you offer video production in Los Angeles with a film crew?
faqs.a: No. We do not send crews or run a local studio, and we are upfront about that in every quote for video production. Los Angeles clients get animation, motion graphics, editing and AI video, all delivered remotely. If you need live-action filming, your own crew or a production company shoots, and we edit, animate and version the footage.

faqs.q: Can you edit footage we shoot ourselves in LA?
faqs.a: Yes, and many clients work this way. You upload footage through a cloud transfer tool, we cut it overnight Pacific time, and you review with time-coded comments. We handle color correction, sound clean-up, titles, captions and versions for each platform.

faqs.q: Is AI video safe to use for our brand?
faqs.a: It can be, with clear rules. We only use real people's likenesses with written consent, label AI-generated content, review every output by hand and keep records of tools used. We usually recommend AI for ad variations, backgrounds and scenes rather than replacing presenters or performers.

faqs.q: How fast can you turn around social videos?
faqs.a: It depends on volume and complexity, but because our teams work while Los Angeles sleeps, simple edits are often ready for review the next morning. For ongoing work we agree a weekly schedule and delivery times in writing, and the Signal Lead tracks every deadline.

faqs.q: What formats and versions do you deliver?
faqs.a: Whatever the channels need: vertical 9:16 for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, square and 4:5 for feeds, 16:9 for YouTube and websites, plus captioned and silent versions. We also deliver project files and graphics templates on request, so your in-house team can make quick changes without coming back to us.

faqs.q: Do you make animated explainers for health tech and medical companies?
faqs.a: Yes. Animation is often better than filming for medical subjects because it can show what happens inside the body or a device clearly, and avoids filming patients. Your clinical team reviews the script and storyboard for accuracy before animation starts.

faqs.q: Can you provide a managed editing team for our content calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. We already run a managed video editing team for a US client, with one lead handling briefs, quality checks and deadlines, and we can set one up around your content calendar. It suits LA brands and media companies whose video volume has outgrown their in-house editors.
